article_notes: Survey of 242 police K9 dogs at one kennel unit in Egypt (2017-2019); 62 Babesia-positive on smear, B. vogeli identified by 18S rRNA sequencing of three specimens only; 28 of the 62 co-infected with E. canis (method of E. canis detection not described). Table 1 records each dog's status as live or died; cause and timing of death and any euthanasia are not stated. The only result within infected dogs against an outcome is E. canis co-infection vs live/died status (Table 1, mixed infection column; FET p=0.065). Note that Table 1 percentages in the 'Babesia infected' column are row-wise (e.g. 9 (3.72) for live dogs looks miscalculated); the counts are used. All haematology, biochemistry, oxidative stress, CRP and cytokine results (Tables 2 and 3) compare infected with healthy dogs (or single vs mixed infection, which is not severity) and were not extracted. Infection rate vs live/died across all 242 dogs is an infected vs non-infected comparison and was not extracted.

severity_definitions.label: died vs live
severity_definitions.definition: Dog status recorded as died or live in Table 1 (police dog survey). Among the 62 Babesia-infected dogs, 53 died and 9 were alive. Cause of death, follow-up period and euthanasia not stated.

associations.marker_as_reported: mixed infection with Ehrlichia (E. canis co-infection)
associations.statistic: 26 (49.06%) of dead vs 1 (11.11%) of live infected dogs had mixed infection; Fisher's exact test
associations.quote: No significant association was observed between the breed of dogs (p=0.858; FET), sex (p=0.530; FET), alive or dead status (p=0.065; FET)
